== extVar | 0.10.0 | std-extVar
<p>If an external variable with the given name was defined, return its value. Otherwise, raise an error.</p>
== thisFile | 0.10.0 | std-thisFile
<p>Note that this is a field. It contains the current Jsonnet filename as a string.</p>
== type | 0.10.0 | std-type
<p>Return a string that indicates the type of the value. The possible return values are: "array", "boolean", "function", "null", "number", "object", and "string".</p>
<p>The following functions are also available and return a boolean: <code>std.isArray(v)</code>, <code>std.isBoolean(v)</code>, <code>std.isFunction(v)</code>, <code>std.isNumber(v)</code>, <code>std.isObject(v)</code>, and <code>std.isString(v)</code>.</p>
== length | 0.10.0 | std-length
<p>Depending on the type of the value given, either returns the number of elements in the array, the number of codepoints in the string, the number of parameters in the function, or the number of fields in the object. Raises an error if given a primitive value, i.e. <code>null</code>, <code>true</code> or <code>false</code>.</p>
== prune | 0.10.0 | std-prune
<p>Recursively remove all "empty" members of <code>a</code>. "Empty" is defined as zero length `arrays`, zero length `objects`, or `null` values. The argument <code>a</code> may have any type.</p>
== isNull | 0.22.0 | std-isNull
<p>Returns true if the given value is null, false otherwise.</p>
== clamp | 0.15.0 | std-clamp
<p>Clamp a value to fit within the range [<code>minVal</code>, <code>maxVal</code>]. Equivalent to <code>std.max(minVal, std.min(x, maxVal))</code>.</p>
== assertEqual | 0.10.0 | std-assertEqual
<p>Ensure that <code>a == b</code>. Returns <code>true</code> or throws an error message.</p>
== toString | 0.10.0 | std-toString
<p>Convert the given argument to a string.</p>
== codepoint | 0.10.0 | std-codepoint
<p>Returns the positive integer representing the unicode codepoint of the character in the given single-character string. This function is the inverse of <code>std.char(n)</code>.</p>
== char | 0.10.0 | std-char
<p>Returns a string of length one whose only unicode codepoint has integer id <code>n</code>. This function is the inverse of <code>std.codepoint(str)</code>.</p>
== substr | 0.10.0 | std-substr
<p>Returns a string that is the part of <code>str</code> that starts at offset <code>from</code> and is <code>len</code> codepoints long. If the string <code>str</code> is shorter than <code>from+len</code>, the suffix starting at position <code>from</code> will be returned.</p>
<p>The slice operator (e.g., <code>str[from:to]</code>) can also be used on strings, as an alternative to this function. However, note that the slice operator takes a start and an end index, but <code>std.substr</code> takes a start index and a length.</p>
== findSubstr | 0.10.0 | std-findSubstr
<p>Returns an array that contains the indexes of all occurrences of <code>pat</code> in <code>str</code>.</p>
== startsWith | 0.10.0 | std-startsWith
<p>Returns whether the string a is prefixed by the string b.</p>
== endsWith | 0.10.0 | std-endsWith
<p>Returns whether the string a is suffixed by the string b.</p>
== stripChars | 0.15.0 | std-stripChars
<p>Removes characters <code>chars</code> from the beginning and from the end of <code>str</code>.</p>
== lstripChars | 0.15.0 | std-lstripChars
<p>Removes characters <code>chars</code> from the beginning of <code>str</code>.</p>
== rstripChars | 0.15.0 | std-rstripChars
<p>Removes characters <code>chars</code> from the end of <code>str</code>.</p>
== split | 0.10.0 | std-split
<p>Split the string <code>str</code> into an array of strings, divided by the string <code>c</code>.</p>
<p>Note: Versions up to and including 0.18.0 require <code>c</code> to be a single character.</p>
== splitLimit | 0.10.0 | std-splitLimit
<p>As <code>std.split(str, c)</code> but will stop after <code>maxsplits</code> splits, thereby the largest array it will return has length <code>maxsplits + 1</code>. A limit of <code>-1</code> means unlimited.</p>
<p>Note: Versions up to and including 0.18.0 require <code>c</code> to be a single character.</p>
== splitLimitR | 0.19.0 | std-splitLimitR
<p>As <code>std.splitLimit(str, c, maxsplits)</code> but will split from right to left.</p>
== strReplace | 0.10.0 | std-strReplace
<p>Returns a copy of the string in which all occurrences of string <code>from</code> have been replaced with string <code>to</code>.</p>
== isEmpty | 0.20.0 | std-isEmpty
<p>Returns true if the given string is of zero length.</p>
== trim | 0.21.0 | std-trim
<p>Returns a copy of string after eliminating leading and trailing whitespaces.</p>
== equalsIgnoreCase | 0.21.0 | std-equalsIgnoreCase
<p>Returns true if the the given <code>str1</code> is equal to <code>str2</code> by doing case insensitive comparison, false otherwise.</p>
== asciiUpper | 0.10.0 | std-asciiUpper
<p>Returns a copy of the string in which all ASCII letters are capitalized.</p>
== asciiLower | 0.10.0 | std-asciiLower
<p>Returns a copy of the string in which all ASCII letters are lower cased.</p>
== stringChars | 0.10.0 | std-stringChars
<p>Split the string <code>str</code> into an array of strings, each containing a single codepoint.</p>
== format | 0.10.0 | std-format
<p>Format the string <code>str</code> using the values in <code>vals</code>. The values can be an array, an object, or in other cases are treated as if they were provided in a singleton array. The string formatting follows the <a href="https://docs.python.org/2/library/stdtypes.html#string-formatting">same rules</a> as Python. The <code>%</code> operator can be used as a shorthand for this function.</p>
== escapeStringBash | 0.10.0 | std-escapeStringBash
<p>Wrap <code>str</code> in single quotes, and escape any single quotes within <code>str</code> by changing them to a sequence <code>'"'"'</code>. This allows injection of arbitrary strings as arguments of commands in bash scripts.</p>
== escapeStringDollars | 0.10.0 | std-escapeStringDollars
<p>Convert $ to $$ in <code>str</code>. This allows injection of arbitrary strings into systems that use $ for string interpolation (like Terraform).</p>
== escapeStringJson | 0.10.0 | std-escapeStringJson
<p>Convert <code>str</code> to allow it to be embedded in a JSON representation, within a string. This adds quotes, escapes backslashes, and escapes unprintable characters.</p>
== escapeStringPython | 0.10.0 | std-escapeStringPython
<p>Convert <code>str</code> to allow it to be embedded in Python. This is an alias for <code>std.escapeStringJson</code>.</p>
== escapeStringXML | 0.10.0 | std-escapeStringXml
<p>Convert <code>str</code> to allow it to be embedded in XML (or HTML). The following replacements are made:</p>
<pre>{
  "&lt;": "&amp;lt;",
  "&gt;": "&amp;gt;",
  "&amp;": "&amp;amp;",
  "\"": "&amp;quot;",
  "'": "&amp;apos;",
}</pre>
== parseInt | 0.10.0 | std-parseInt
<p>Parses a signed decimal integer from the input string.</p>
== parseOctal | 0.10.0 | std-parseOctal
<p>Parses an unsigned octal integer from the input string. Initial zeroes are tolerated.</p>
== parseHex | 0.10.0 | std-parseHex
<p>Parses an unsigned hexadecimal integer, from the input string. Case insensitive.</p>
== parseJson | 0.13.0 | std-parseJson
<p>Parses a JSON string.</p>
== parseYaml | 0.18.0 | std-parseYaml
<p>Parses a YAML string. This is provided as a "best-effort" mechanism and should not be relied on to provide a fully standards compliant YAML parser. YAML is a superset of JSON, consequently "downcasting" or manifestation of YAML into JSON or Jsonnet values will only succeed when using the subset of YAML that is compatible with JSON. The parser does not support YAML documents with scalar values at the root. The root node of a YAML document must start with either a YAML sequence or map to be successfully parsed.</p>
== encodeUTF8 | 0.13.0 | std-encodeUTF8
<p>Encode a string using <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTF-8">UTF8</a>. Returns an array of numbers representing bytes.</p>
== decodeUTF8 | 0.13.0 | std-decodeUTF8
<p>Decode an array of numbers representing bytes using <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTF-8">UTF8</a>. Returns a string.</p>
== manifestIni | 0.10.0 | std-manifestIni
<p>Convert the given structure to a string in <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INI_file">INI format</a>. This allows using Jsonnet's object model to build a configuration to be consumed by an application expecting an INI file. The data is in the form of a set of sections, each containing a key/value mapping. These examples should make it clear:</p>
<pre>{
    main: { a: "1", b: "2" },
    sections: {
        s1: {x: "11", y: "22", z: "33"},
        s2: {p: "yes", q: ""},
        empty: {},
    }
}</pre>
<p>Yields a string containing this INI file:</p>
<pre>a = 1
b = 2
[empty]
[s1]
x = 11
y = 22
z = 33
[s2]
p = yes
q =</pre>
== manifestPython | 0.10.0 | std-manifestPython
<p>Convert the given value to a JSON-like form that is compatible with Python. The chief differences are True / False / None instead of true / false / null.</p>
<pre>{
    b: ["foo", "bar"],
    c: true,
    d: null,
    e: { f1: false, f2: 42 },
}</pre>
<p>Yields a string containing Python code like:</p>
<pre>{
    "b": ["foo", "bar"],
    "c": True,
    "d": None,
    "e": {"f1": False, "f2": 42}
}</pre>
== manifestPythonVars | 0.10.0 | std-manifestPythonVars
<p>Convert the given object to a JSON-like form that is compatible with Python. The key difference to <code>std.manifestPython</code> is that the top level is represented as a list of Python global variables.</p>
<pre>{
    b: ["foo", "bar"],
    c: true,
    d: null,
    e: { f1: false, f2: 42 },
}</pre>
<p>Yields a string containing this Python code:</p>
<pre>b = ["foo", "bar"]
c = True
d = None
e = {"f1": False, "f2": 42}</pre>
== manifestJsonEx | 0.10.0 | std-manifestJsonEx
<p>Convert the given object to a JSON form. <code>indent</code> is a string containing one or more whitespaces that are used for indentation. <code>newline</code> is by default <code>\n</code> and is inserted where a newline would normally be used to break long lines. <code>key_val_sep</code> is used to separate the key and value of an object field:</p>
<pre>std.manifestJsonEx(
{
    x: [1, 2, 3, true, false, null,
        "string\nstring"],
    y: { a: 1, b: 2, c: [1, 2] },
}, "    ")</pre>
<p>Yields a string containing this JSON:</p>
<pre>{
    "x": [
        1,
        2,
        3,
        true,
        false,
        null,
        "string\nstring"
    ],
    "y": {
        "a": 1,
        "b": 2,
        "c": [
            1,
            2
        ]
    }
}</pre>
<pre>std.manifestJsonEx(
{
  x: [1, 2, "string\nstring"],
  y: { a: 1, b: [1, 2] },
}, "", " ", " : ")</pre>
<p>Yields a string containing this JSON:</p>
<pre>{ "x" : [ 1, 2, "string\nstring" ], "y" : { "a" : 1, "b" : [ 1, 2 ] } }</pre>
== manifestJson | 0.10.0 | std-manifestJson
<p>Convert the given object to a JSON form. Under the covers, it calls <code>std.manifestJsonEx</code> with a 4-space indent:</p>
<pre>std.manifestJson(
{
    x: [1, 2, 3, true, false, null,
        "string\nstring"],
    y: { a: 1, b: 2, c: [1, 2] },
})</pre>
<p>Yields a string containing this JSON:</p>
<pre>{
    "x": [
        1,
        2,
        3,
        true,
        false,
        null,
        "string\nstring"
    ],
    "y": {
        "a": 1,
        "b": 2,
        "c": [
            1,
            2
        ]
    }
}</pre>
== manifestJsonMinified | 0.18.0 | std-manifestJsonMinified
<p>Convert the given object to a minified JSON form. Under the covers, it calls <code>std.manifestJsonEx</code>:</p>
<pre>std.manifestJsonMinified(
{
    x: [1, 2, 3, true, false, null,
        "string\nstring"],
    y: { a: 1, b: 2, c: [1, 2] },
})</pre>
<p>Yields a string containing this JSON:</p>
<pre>{"x":[1,2,3,true,false,null,"string\nstring"],"y":{"a":1,"b":2,"c":[1,2]}}</pre>
== manifestYamlDoc | 0.10.0 | std-manifestYamlDoc
<p>Convert the given value to a YAML form. Note that <code>std.manifestJson</code> could also be used for this purpose, because any JSON is also valid YAML. But this function will produce more canonical-looking YAML.</p>
<pre>std.manifestYamlDoc(
  {
      x: [1, 2, 3, true, false, null,
          "string\nstring\n"],
      y: { a: 1, b: 2, c: [1, 2] },
  },
  indent_array_in_object=false)</pre>
<p>Yields a string containing this YAML:</p>
<pre>"x":
  - 1
  - 2
  - 3
  - true
  - false
  - null
  - |
      string
      string
"y":
  "a": 1
  "b": 2
  "c":
      - 1
      - 2</pre>
<p>The <code>indent_array_in_object</code> param adds additional indentation which some people may find easier to read.</p>
<p>The <code>quote_keys</code> parameter controls whether YAML identifiers are always quoted or only when necessary.</p>
== manifestYamlStream | 0.10.0 | std-manifestYamlStream
<p>Given an array of values, emit a YAML "stream", which is a sequence of documents separated by <code>---</code> and ending with <code>...</code>.</p>
<pre>std.manifestYamlStream(
  ['a', 1, []],
  indent_array_in_object=false,
  c_document_end=true)</pre>
<p>Yields this string:</p>
<pre>---
"a"
---
1
---
[]
...</pre>
<p>The <code>indent_array_in_object</code> and <code>quote_keys</code> params are the same as in <code>manifestYamlDoc</code>.</p>
<p>The <code>c_document_end</code> param adds the optional terminating <code>...</code>.</p>
== manifestXmlJsonml | 0.10.0 | std-manifestXmlJsonml
<p>Convert the given <a href="http://www.jsonml.org/">JsonML</a>-encoded value to a string containing the XML.</p>
<pre>std.manifestXmlJsonml([
    'svg', { height: 100, width: 100 },
    [
        'circle', {
        cx: 50, cy: 50, r: 40,
        stroke: 'black', 'stroke-width': 3,
        fill: 'red',
        }
    ],
])</pre>
<p>Yields a string containing this XML (all on one line):</p>
<pre>&lt;svg height="100" width="100"&gt;
    &lt;circle cx="50" cy="50" fill="red" r="40"
    stroke="black" stroke-width="3"&gt;&lt;/circle&gt;;
&lt;/svg&gt;;</pre>
<p>Which represents the following image:</p>
<p>JsonML is designed to preserve "mixed-mode content" (i.e., textual data outside of or next to elements). This includes the whitespace needed to avoid having all the XML on one line, which is meaningful in XML. In order to have whitespace in the XML output, it must be present in the JsonML input:</p>
<pre>std.manifestXmlJsonml([
    'svg',
    { height: 100, width: 100 },
    '\n  ',
    [
        'circle',
        {
        cx: 50, cy: 50, r: 40, stroke: 'black',
        'stroke-width': 3, fill: 'red',
        }
    ],
    '\n',
])</pre>
== manifestTomlEx | 0.18.0 | std-manifestTomlEx
<p>Convert the given object to a TOML form. <code>indent</code> is a string containing one or more whitespaces that are used for indentation:</p>
<pre>std.manifestTomlEx({
  key1: "value",
  key2: 1,
  section: {
    a: 1,
    b: "str",
    c: false,
    d: [1, "s", [2, 3]],
    subsection: {
      k: "v",
    },
  },
  sectionArray: [
    { k: "v1", v: 123 },
    { k: "v2", c: "value2" },
  ],
}, "  ")</pre>
<p>Yields a string containing this TOML file:</p>
<pre>key1 = "value"
key2 = 1
[section]
  a = 1
  b = "str"
  c = false
  d = [
    1,
    "s",
    [ 2, 3 ]
  ]
  [section.subsection]
    k = "v"
[[sectionArray]]
  k = "v1"
  v = 123
[[sectionArray]]
  c = "value2"
  k = "v2"</pre>
== makeArray | 0.10.0 | std-makeArray
<p>Create a new array of <code>sz</code> elements by calling <code>func(i)</code> to initialize each element. Func is expected to be a function that takes a single parameter, the index of the element it should initialize.</p>
== member | 0.15.0 | std-member
<p>Returns whether <code>x</code> occurs in <code>arr</code>. Argument <code>arr</code> may be an array or a string.</p>
== count | 0.10.0 | std-count
<p>Return the number of times that <code>x</code> occurs in <code>arr</code>.</p>
== find | 0.10.0 | std-find
<p>Returns an array that contains the indexes of all occurrences of <code>value</code> in <code>arr</code>.</p>
== map | 0.10.0 | std-map
<p>Apply the given function to every element of the array to form a new array.</p>
== mapWithIndex | 0.10.0 | std-mapWithIndex
<p>Similar to <a href="https://jsonnet.org/ref/stdlib.html#map">map</a> above, but it also passes to the function the element's index in the array. The function <code>func</code> is expected to take the index as the first parameter and the element as the second.</p>
== filterMap | 0.10.0 | std-filterMap
<p>It first filters, then maps the given array, using the two functions provided.</p>
== flatMap | 0.10.0 | std-flatMap
<p>Apply the given function to every element of <code>arr</code> to form a new array then flatten the result. The argument <code>arr</code> must be an array or a string. If <code>arr</code> is an array, function <code>func</code> must return an array. If <code>arr</code> is a string, function <code>func</code> must return an string.</p>
<p>The <code>std.flatMap</code> function can be thought of as a generalized <code>std.map</code>, with each element mapped to 0, 1 or more elements.</p>
== filter | 0.10.0 | std-filter
<p>Return a new array containing all the elements of <code>arr</code> for which the <code>func</code> function returns true.</p>
== foldl | 0.10.0 | std-foldl
<p>Classic foldl function. Calls the function for each array element, passing the result from the previous call (or <code>init</code> for the first call), and the array element. Traverses the array from left to right.</p>
<p>For example: <code>foldl(f, [1,2,3], 0)</code> is equivalent to <code>f(f(f(0, 1), 2), 3)</code>.</p>
== foldr | 0.10.0 | std-foldr
<p>Classic foldr function. Calls the function for each array element, passing the array element and the result from the previous call (or <code>init</code> for the first call). Traverses the array from right to left.</p>
<p>For example: <code>foldr(f, [1,2,3], 0)</code> is equivalent to <code>f(1, f(2, f(3, 0)))</code>.</p>
== range | 0.10.0 | std-range
<p>Return an array of ascending numbers between the two limits, inclusively.</p>
== repeat | 0.15.0 | std-repeat
<p>Repeats an array or a string <code>what</code> a number of times specified by an integer <code>count</code>.</p>
== slice | 0.10.0 | std-slice
<p>Selects the elements of an array or a string from <code>index</code> to <code>end</code> with <code>step</code> and returns an array or a string respectively.</p>
<p>Note that it's recommended to use dedicated slicing syntax both for arrays and strings (e.g. <code>arr[0:4:1]</code> instead of <code>std.slice(arr, 0, 4, 1)</code>).</p>
== join | 0.10.0 | std-join
<p>If <code>sep</code> is a string, then <code>arr</code> must be an array of strings, in which case they are concatenated with <code>sep</code> used as a delimiter. If <code>sep</code> is an array, then <code>arr</code> must be an array of arrays, in which case the arrays are concatenated in the same way, to produce a single array.</p>
== deepJoin | 0.10.0 | std-deepJoin
<p>Concatenate an array containing strings and arrays to form a single string. If <code>arr</code> is a string, it is returned unchanged. If it is an array, it is flattened and the string elements are concatenated together with no separator.</p>
== lines | 0.10.0 | std-lines
<p>Concatenate an array of strings into a text file with newline characters after each string. This is suitable for constructing bash scripts and the like.</p>
== flattenArrays | 0.10.0 | std-flattenArrays
<p>Concatenate an array of arrays into a single array.</p>
== flattenDeepArray | 0.21.0 | std-flattenDeepArray
<p>Concatenate an array containing values and arrays into a single flattened array.</p>
== reverse | 0.13.0 | std-reverse
<p>Reverses an array.</p>
== sort | 0.10.0 | std-sort
<p>Sorts the array using the &lt;= operator.</p>
<p>Optional argument <code>keyF</code> is a single argument function used to extract comparison key from each array element. Default value is identity function <code>keyF=function(x) x</code>.</p>
== uniq | 0.10.0 | std-uniq
<p>Removes successive duplicates. When given a sorted array, removes all duplicates.</p>
<p>Optional argument <code>keyF</code> is a single argument function used to extract comparison key from each array element. Default value is identity function <code>keyF=function(x) x</code>.</p>
== all | 0.19.0 | std-all
<p>Return true if all elements of <code>arr</code> is true, false otherwise. <code>all([])</code> evaluates to true.</p>
<p>It's an error if 1) <code>arr</code> is not an array, or 2) <code>arr</code> contains non-boolean values.</p>
== any | 0.19.0 | std-any
<p>Return true if any element of <code>arr</code> is true, false otherwise. <code>any([])</code> evaluates to false.</p>
<p>It's an error if 1) <code>arr</code> is not an array, or 2) <code>arr</code> contains non-boolean values.</p>
== sum | 0.20.0 | std-sum
<p>Return sum of all element in <code>arr</code>.</p>
== minArray | 0.21.0 | std-minArray
<p>Return the minimum of all elements in <code>arr</code>. If <code>keyF</code> is provided, it is called on each element of the array and should return a comparator value, and in this case <code>minArray</code> will return an element with the minimum comparator value. If <code>onEmpty</code> is provided, and <code>arr</code> is empty, then <code>minArray</code> will return the provided <code>onEmpty</code> value. If <code>onEmpty</code> is not provided, then an empty <code>arr</code> will raise an error.</p>
== maxArray | 0.21.0 | std-maxArray
<p>Return the maximum of all elements in <code>arr</code>. If <code>keyF</code> is provided, it is called on each element of the array and should return a comparator value, and in this case <code>maxArray</code> will return an element with the maximum comparator value. If <code>onEmpty</code> is provided, and <code>arr</code> is empty, then <code>maxArray</code> will return the provided <code>onEmpty</code> value. If <code>onEmpty</code> is not provided, then an empty <code>arr</code> will raise an error.</p>
== contains | 0.21.0 | std-contains
<p>Return true if given <code>elem</code> is present in <code>arr</code>, false otherwise.</p>
== avg | 0.21.0 | std-avg
<p>Return average of all element in <code>arr</code>.</p>
== remove | 0.21.0 | std-remove
<p>Remove first occurrence of <code>elem</code> from <code>arr</code>.</p>
== removeAt | 0.21.0 | std-removeAt
<p>Remove element at <code>idx</code> index from <code>arr</code>.</p>
== set | 0.10.0 | std-set
<p>Shortcut for std.uniq(std.sort(arr)).</p>
== setInter | 0.10.0 | std-setInter
<p>Set intersection operation (values in both a and b).</p>
== setUnion | 0.10.0 | std-setUnion
<p>Set union operation (values in any of <code>a</code> or <code>b</code>). Note that + on sets will simply concatenate the arrays, possibly forming an array that is not a set (due to not being ordered without duplicates).</p>
== setDiff | 0.10.0 | std-setDiff
<p>Set difference operation (values in a but not b).</p>
== setMember | 0.10.0 | std-setMember
<p>Returns <code>true</code> if x is a member of array, otherwise <code>false</code>.</p>
== get | 0.18.0 | std-get
<p>Returns the object's field if it exists or default value otherwise. <code>inc_hidden</code> controls whether to include hidden fields.</p>
== objectHas | 0.10.0 | std-objectHas
<p>Returns <code>true</code> if the given object has the field (given as a string), otherwise <code>false</code>. Raises an error if the arguments are not object and string respectively. Returns false if the field is hidden.</p>
== objectFields | 0.10.0 | std-objectFields
<p>Returns an array of strings, each element being a field from the given object. Does not include hidden fields.</p>
== objectValues | 0.17.0 | std-objectValues
<p>Returns an array of the values in the given object. Does not include hidden fields.</p>
== objectKeysValues | 0.20.0 | std-objectKeysValues
<p>Returns an array of objects from the given object, each object having two fields: <code>key</code> (string) and <code>value</code> (object). Does not include hidden fields.</p>
== objectHasAll | 0.10.0 | std-objectHasAll
<p>As <code>std.objectHas</code> but also includes hidden fields.</p>
== objectFieldsAll | 0.10.0 | std-objectFieldsAll
<p>As <code>std.objectFields</code> but also includes hidden fields.</p>
== objectValuesAll | 0.17.0 | std-objectValuesAll
<p>As <code>std.objectValues</code> but also includes hidden fields.</p>
== objectKeysValuesAll | 0.20.0 | std-objectKeysValuesAll
<p>As <code>std.objectKeysValues</code> but also includes hidden fields.</p>
== objectRemoveKey | 0.21.0 | std-objectRemoveKey
<p>Returns a new object after removing the given key from object.</p>
== mapWithKey | 0.10.0 | std-mapWithKey
<p>Apply the given function to all fields of the given object, also passing the field name. The function <code>func</code> is expected to take the field name as the first parameter and the field value as the second.</p>
== base64 | 0.10.0 | std-base64
<p>Encodes the given value into a base64 string. The encoding sequence is <code>A-Za-z0-9+/</code> with <code>=</code> to pad the output to a multiple of 4 characters. The value can be a string or an array of numbers, but the codepoints / numbers must be in the 0 to 255 range. The resulting string has no line breaks.</p>
== base64DecodeBytes | 0.10.0 | std-base64DecodeBytes
<p>Decodes the given base64 string into an array of bytes (number values). Currently assumes the input string has no linebreaks and is padded to a multiple of 4 (with the = character). In other words, it consumes the output of std.base64().</p>
== base64Decode | 0.10.0 | std-base64Decode
<p><em>Deprecated, use <code>std.base64DecodeBytes</code> and decode the string explicitly (e.g. with <code>std.decodeUTF8</code>) instead.</em></p>
<p>Behaves like std.base64DecodeBytes() except returns a naively encoded string instead of an array of bytes.</p>
== md5 | 0.10.0 | std-md5
<p>Encodes the given value into an MD5 string.</p>
== sha1 | 0.21.0 | std-sha1
<p>Encodes the given value into an SHA1 string.</p>
<p>This function is only available in Go version of jsonnet.</p>
== sha256 | 0.21.0 | std-sha256
<p>Encodes the given value into an SHA256 string.</p>
<p>This function is only available in Go version of jsonnet.</p>
== sha512 | 0.21.0 | std-sha512
<p>Encodes the given value into an SHA512 string.</p>
<p>This function is only available in Go version of jsonnet.</p>
== sha3 | 0.21.0 | std-sha3
<p>Encodes the given value into an SHA3 string.</p>
<p>This function is only available in Go version of jsonnet.</p>
== xor | 0.20.0 | std-xor
<p>Returns the xor of the two given booleans.</p>
== xnor | 0.20.0 | std-xnor
<p>Returns the xnor of the two given booleans.</p>
== mergePatch | 0.10.0 | std-mergePatch
<p>Applies <code>patch</code> to <code>target</code> according to <a href="https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396">RFC7396</a></p>
== trace | 0.11.0 | std-trace
<p>Outputs the given string <code>str</code> to stderr and returns <code>rest</code> as the result.</p>
<pre>local conditionalReturn(cond, in1, in2) =
  if (cond) then
      std.trace('cond is true returning '
              + std.toString(in1), in1)
  else
      std.trace('cond is false returning '
              + std.toString(in2), in2);
{
    a: conditionalReturn(true, { b: true }, { c: false }),
}</pre>
<p>Prints:</p>
<pre>TRACE: test.jsonnet:3 cond is true returning {"b": true}
{
    "a": {
        "b": true
    }
}</pre>
